name: George Orwell
summary: Orwell described himself as a democratic socialist who opposed totalitarianism of left and right. He favoured nationalising major industry, capping incomes and ending class and hereditary privilege, backed revolution understood as a shift of power rather than a class dictatorship, and rejected pacifism, imperialism and nationalism while defending a patriotism tied to English life.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He calls pure pacifism negative and irresponsible and the by-product of naval power, and he spells out that real pacifism would mean letting the Nazis win.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He adds abolition of all hereditary privilege, especially in education, to his definition of socialism, and expects a revolution to abolish the House of Lords.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He says money for internal purposes would become a ration coupon but also that without some money reward there is no incentive for certain jobs, so wages stay.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: His programme limits and equalises pay, not abolishes it; he states that a money reward is needed to get certain jobs done.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He says the process of mechanisation is out of control and that we should treat new inventions as the King of Brobdingnag treated gunpowder.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Land is listed with mines, ships and machinery among productive goods that his socialism vests in the State.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He says if England were overrun the English people would know they were beaten and would continue the struggle, but he does not call such resistance justified in general.

central-planning.rationale: Part II of The Lion and the Unicorn says a socialist State that calculates the goods needed can solve the problems of production and consumption that capitalism cannot, though he is not sure socialism is superior in every way.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He says Britain has artificially kept India backward and proposes equal partnership with a right to secede, though he also holds that Indian administration still needs British experts for years.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He calls the old-fashioned proletarian revolution an impossibility in England and says patriotism is stronger than class hatred, which cuts against class conflict as the main driver of history.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He says the European peoples must stop being exploiters abroad and that colonies in Africa and the Middle East should become autonomous republics equal with the European peoples.

conscription.rationale: He writes that Britain nearly perished in 1940 for lack of a large army that conscription introduced three years earlier would have provided.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says the mass of people must have some kind of control over the government for common ownership to mean anything.

death-penalty.rationale: His essay A Hanging presents the execution of a healthy man as a wrong, though he never sets out a policy on capital punishment.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He treats the Communists and pacifists who opposed the war against Hitler as pro-Fascist and wants the war won, as a revolutionary war.

democracy-best.rationale: He makes political democracy part of what socialism means and calls himself a democratic socialist, but does not discuss democracy when voters choose badly.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He writes that revolution "does not mean the dictatorship of a single class" and that the people who can carry out change come from all classes.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In Marrakech he asks whether the colonised are "the same flesh" as the colonisers and treats the empire as founded on denying it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism for him requires approximate equality of incomes, though he says exact equality is unrealistic because some money reward is needed.

gradual-change.rationale: He calls for a rapid fundamental shift of power and says time presses, though in an English, non-doctrinaire style that keeps some old forms such as the Monarchy.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: State ownership is meant to eliminate the class of mere owners who live by title-deeds and share certificates, so that nobody lives without working.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: In Toward European Unity he says the British worker lives above his income by world standards because of exploitation of coloured peoples, and The Lion and the Unicorn says trade-union wages depended indirectly on the sweating of Indian coolies.

leader-cult.rationale: Reviewing a book on Russia he lists the "oriental worship of Stalin", the muzzled press and the purges among the developments he sees as political failures.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: He says state ownership implies nobody shall live without working, aimed at the idle owning class, but he does not propose a general legal duty.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He argues that private capitalism "does not work" and cannot deliver the goods, leaving wasted surplus and unemployment in peace and shortage in war.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: Point two of his programme limits incomes so that the highest does not exceed the lowest by more than ten to one.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: In Antisemitism in Britain he treats stories blaming the Jews, such as for the 1943 Underground crush, as absurdities that antisemites readily believe.

nation-first.rationale: Notes on Nationalism condemns nationalism as the pursuit of power and prestige for the nation, and his programme favours an imperial council and a European federation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wants the State to own land, mines, railways, banks and major industry and to limit incomes, far beyond defence, justice and property protection.

one-party-rule.rationale: He lists political democracy as a necessary safeguard of socialism and warns that the State can come to mean a self-elected political party, letting oligarchy return.

party-controls-media.rationale: The same essay defends intellectual liberty against government and party control of what may be printed, and calls the muzzled press a mark of Soviet dictatorship.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He argues patriotism has become a tremendous lever for socialists and wants a movement that brings patriotism and intelligence together to serve working people.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In Toward European Unity (1947) he argues democratic socialism must be made to work in a Socialist United States of Europe, and that Britain should join in as the first step.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He defines patriotism as devotion to a particular place and way of life and says England must be true to herself, while rejecting nationalism.

production-for-use.rationale: He contrasts a socialist economy that works out what goods are needed with capitalism run for profit, and describes "private profit" as pulling against public necessity.

property-fundamental.rationale: He keeps personal possessions private but wants all productive property vested in the State, so he does not treat property rights as something to be very hard to override.

public-ownership.rationale: The Lion and the Unicorn (part III) proposes nationalization of land, mines, railways, banks and major industries as the first point of a six-point programme, and calls it the necessary first step.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In a 1944 Tribune column he attacks colour bars, says there is no legal disability against coloured people in Britain, and urges public protest whenever one appears.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pacifism, he says, can only appeal to people in sheltered positions and is objectively pro-Fascist; he himself served in the Spanish militia.

state-harmful.rationale: His socialism is built on a State that owns the major means of production on behalf of the people, the opposite of treating the state as unnecessary.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He proposes a European socialist union able to stand against both Russia and America, and says Britain can only escape dependence on the US by giving up being an extra-European power, though he would choose America if forced.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In The Prevention of Literature he says freedom of the press, if it means anything, means the freedom to criticise and oppose, and he condemns totalitarian suppression.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He wants the highest tax-free income held to ten times the lowest, and says workers who are taxed and overworked must see the rich hit even harder.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Road to Wigan Pier treats worship of mechanical progress as a vulgar illusion and says the machine should be accepted grudgingly, like a drug.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He calls patriotism defensive by nature and says the abiding purpose of nationalism is to gain more power and prestige for the nation.

total-state.rationale: Every serious line he wrote since 1936 was, he says, against totalitarianism and for democratic socialism.

unions-good.rationale: He credits the trade unions with part of the rise in the working class standard of living and treats the Labour Party as their creature, while criticising its parochialism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He writes that England is governed by the rich and by birth, that "the rule of money" breeds incompetence, and that centralised ownership matters only if people live at a roughly equal level.

notes: Mature position is the democratic socialism of 1936-1950; the 1928-29 reformist views are earlier. Themes searched: economy, empire, war and pacifism, race, press freedom, Europe, technology. Few statements on gender, family, religion and environment have a stated position.
